results.location: Preliminaries
results.content: Forward OU SDE (Eq. 1): $$\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x} = -\mathbf{x}(t)\mathrm{d}t + \mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(t),$$ where $\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(t)$ is the square root of two times a Wiener process.
results.route_rationale: Stochastic-process model statement; unformalisable as a crisp formal claim.

math_result.reasoning: Standard Ornstein-Uhlenbeck forward SDE dx = -x dt + dB with dB the square root of two times a Wiener process (diffusion coefficient sqrt(2)). This is the canonical OU process whose stationary distribution is N(0, I_d); the drift -x t and constant diffusion give the correct Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup. No algebraic or sign error. Model statement, not a derived identity; nothing false asserted.

results.location: Preliminaries
results.content: Reverse-time SDE (Eq. 2): $$-\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{x}(t) + 2\mathbf{s}(\mathbf{x}, t)] \mathrm{d}t + \mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(t),$$ where $\mathbf{s}(\mathbf{x}, t) = \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log P_t(\mathbf{x})$.
results.route_rationale: Reverse-time diffusion (Anderson); model statement, unformalisable here.

math_result.reasoning: Reverse-time SDE. Anderson's reverse-time formula for forward dx = f dt + g dW with f = -x, g^2 = 2 reads dx = [f - g^2 grad log P_t] dt + g dWbar = [-x - 2 grad log P_t] dt + sqrt(2) dWbar. With s = grad log P_t, the paper's -dx = [x + 2s]dt + dB is equivalent to dx = [-x - 2s]dt + (-dB), and -dB has the same law as a Brownian increment. Signs are consistent; no sign-propagation error.

results.location: Preliminaries
results.content: Score-matching loss (Eq. 3): $$\hat{\mathbf{s}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = \arg \min_{\mathbf{s}} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}\sim P_0, \boldsymbol{\xi}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_d)} \left[ \left\| \sqrt{\Delta_t}\mathbf{s}(\mathbf{x}(t), t) + \boldsymbol{\xi} \right\|^2 \right],$$ with $\Delta_t = 1 - e^{-2t}$.
results.route_rationale: Denoising score-matching objective; the argmin-equals-score claim rests on heavy probability, unformalisable here.

math_result.reasoning: Denoising score-matching objective. Since grad log P_t(x_t|x_0) = -(x_t - e^{-t}x_0)/Delta_t = -xi/sqrt(Delta_t), the squared loss ||sqrt(Delta_t) s + xi||^2 equals Delta_t ||s - grad log P_t(.|x_0)||^2 up to an x_0-independent constant. The conditional minimizer is s*(x_t) = -E[xi|x_t]/sqrt(Delta_t) = grad log P_t(x_t), which is the true score (Vincent 2011). Objective and argmin are correct.

results.location: Preliminaries
results.route_rationale: Definition of the empirical score-matching loss; nothing crisp to prove.

math_result.reasoning: Empirical version of the score-matching loss: replaces the population expectation over x ~ P_0 by the empirical average over the n iid samples x^nu, and x_t^nu(xi) = e^{-t}x^nu + sqrt(Delta_t) xi is the forward noising of sample nu. This is the standard finite-sample score-matching objective; structure and scaling (1/n, Delta_t, sqrt(Delta_t)) match Eq. (3). No error.

results.location: Preliminaries
results.route_rationale: Definition of the empirical forward density; normalization is standard Gaussians, checked informally.

math_result.reasoning: Empirical density of the forward process. Each x^nu(t) = e^{-t}x^nu + sqrt(Delta_t) xi with xi ~ N(0,I_d) is N(e^{-t}x^nu, Delta_t I_d), whose density is (2 pi Delta_t)^{-d/2} exp(-||x - e^{-t}x^nu||^2/(2 Delta_t)). Averaging over nu and normalizing by 1/n gives exactly P_t^emp. The mixture integrates to 1 since each Gaussian is normalized. Correct.

results.location: 2 Generalization and memorization during training of diffusion models
results.content: Memorization criterion (Eq. 6): $E_{x_\tau}[ \|x_\tau - a^{\mu_1}\|_2 / \|x_\tau - a^{\mu_2}\|_2 ] < k$, where $a^{\mu_1}$, $a^{\mu_2}$ are the nearest and second-nearest training-set neighbors of $x_\tau$ in the L2 sense; $k = 1/3$.
results.route_rationale: Experimental/empirical threshold criterion, not a formal theorem.

math_result.reasoning: Heuristic experimental criterion for memorization: a generated sample x_tau is 'memorized' when the expected ratio of distances to its nearest vs second-nearest training-set neighbors is below k = 1/3. This is a thresholding definition adopted from prior numerical work, not a mathematical theorem. The paper explicitly notes the exact values are sensitive to k. Nothing provably false; no algebraic or logical error in the criterion as a definition.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Model definition; no false property asserted.

math_result.reasoning: Definition of the random-features score model s_A(x) = (A/sqrt(p)) sigma(Wx/sqrt(d)), with W in R^{p x d} frozen Gaussian and A in R^{d x p} learned. This is the standard random-features two-layer network. The 1/sqrt(p) scaling on the second layer and 1/sqrt(d) on the features are the conventional normalization choices. Pure definition; no false property asserted.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.content: Test loss and score distance (Eq. 8): $$L_{test} = (1/d)\, \mathbb{E}_{x,\xi}[ \|\sqrt{\Delta_t} s_A(x_t(\xi)) + \xi\|^2 ], \qquad E_{score} = (1/d)\, \mathbb{E}_x[ \|s_A(x) - \nabla \log P_x\|^2 ].$$
results.route_rationale: Definitions of test loss and distance to the exact score.

math_result.reasoning: Definitions of the test loss L_test = (1/d) E[||sqrt(Delta_t) s_A(x_t(xi)) + xi||^2] and the distance-to-exact-score E_score = (1/d) E[||s_A(x) - grad log P_x||^2], with the 1/d rescaling consistent with the finite large-d limit noted in the paper. Both are squared-L2 losses matching the training objective in structure. No error.

math_result.reasoning: Standard gradient-descent update A^{(k+1)} = A^{(k)} - eta grad_A L_train(A^{(k)}). Correct descent direction with learning rate eta. Pure definition of the training dynamics; no error.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Definitions of the correlation matrices U, V used in Eq. (10).

math_result.reasoning: Definitions of the p x p matrix U = (1/n)sum_nu E_xi[sigma(Wx_t^nu/sqrt(d)) sigma(Wx_t^nu/sqrt(d))^T] and the p x d matrix V = (1/n)sum_nu E_xi[sigma(Wx_t^nu/sqrt(d)) xi^T]. These are exactly the correlation matrices that appear in the gradient-flow equation (10); the same xi enters x_t^nu(xi) and the outer factor xi in V, consistent with the loss. Definitions only; no error.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Definitions of Gaussian-integral (Hermite) coefficients.

math_result.reasoning: Definitions of the Gaussian-integral coefficients b_t = E_{u,v}[v sigma(e^{-t} sigma_x u + sqrt(Delta_t) v)] and a_t = E_{u,v}[sigma(e^{-t} sigma_x u + sqrt(Delta_t) v) u/(e^{-t} sigma_x)] over independent standard Gaussians u, v. These are the standard first-order (linear-response) coefficients in the Gaussian universality / GEP analysis. Division by e^{-t} sigma_x is well-defined for sigma_x > 0 (sigma_x^2 = Tr(Sigma)/d), which is the standing assumption. No error.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Definition of the residual variance coefficient.

math_result.reasoning: Definition of v_t^2 = E_{u,v,w}[sigma(e^{-t} sigma_x u + sqrt(Delta_t) v) sigma(e^{-t} sigma_x u + sqrt(Delta_t) w)] - a_t^2 e^{-2t} sigma_x^2, the residual variance of sigma(...) after removing the linear (a_t) part. Consistent with the standard Hermite-decomposition identity E[sigma^2] = a_t^2 e^{-2t} sigma_x^2 + v_t^2 + (b_t^2 + s_t^2). Definition of a moment; no false assertion.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.content: Eq. 14: $$s_t^2 = \mathbb{E}_u\left[\sigma(\Gamma_t u)^2\right] - a_t^2 e^{-2t}\sigma_x^2 - v_t^2 - b_t^2,$$ where $\sigma_x^2 = \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)/d$ and $\Gamma_t = e^{-2t}\sigma_x^2 + \Delta_t = 1 + e^{-2t}(\sigma_x^2 - 1)$.
results.route_rationale: Definition of s_t^2 as residual; the Gamma_t identity is checked informally.

math_result.reasoning: Definition of s_t^2 = E_u[sigma(Gamma_t u)^2] - a_t^2 e^{-2t} sigma_x^2 - v_t^2 - b_t^2, with Gamma_t = e^{-2t} sigma_x^2 + Delta_t = 1 + e^{-2t}(sigma_x^2 - 1). The Gamma_t identity is verified: e^{-2t} sigma_x^2 + (1 - e^{-2t}) = 1 + e^{-2t}(sigma_x^2 - 1) since Delta_t = 1 - e^{-2t}. s_t^2 is defined as the residual, so the equality holds by definition; no error.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Definition of the transformed Stieltjes variable.

math_result.reasoning: Definition of the transformed Stieltjes variable hat s(q) = b_t^2 psi_p + 1/q. This is the standard form of the s-function in random-feature resolvent theory (1/q carries the bare resolvent of the p x p feature matrix, b_t^2 psi_p the mean-field shift). Consistent with the definitions of q and the spectrum. No error.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Definition of the r-correction function.

math_result.reasoning: Definition of hat r(r,q) = psi_p a_t^2 e^{-2t} / (1 + (a_t^2 e^{-2t} psi_p/psi_n) r + (psi_p v_t^2/psi_n) q). The denominator combines the two correction channels (proportional to r and to q) with the correct psi_p/psi_n prefactors, matching the structure expected from linear-pencil theory. Denominator is positive under standing assumptions (a_t^2, v_t^2, psi_p/psi_n >= 0). No error.

The integrand is the resolvent 1/(hat s + lambda hat r), the standard form; rho_Sigma integrates against it with weight 1. Consistent with Eq. (16) and the definitions of q, r, s. results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.route_rationale: Closing self-consistency equation; internal-consistency and large-|z| asymptotics checked informally.

math_result.reasoning: Closing self-consistency equation psi_p(s_t^2 - z) + psi_p v_t^2 / (1 + (a_t^2 e^{-2t} psi_p/psi_n) r + (psi_p v_t^2/psi_n) q) + (1 - psi_p)/q - s/q^2 = 0. The denominator in the second term is exactly the denominator of hat r (Eq. 16), and the (1 - psi_p)/q and -s/q^2 terms are the standard correction terms of the resolvent closure. At large |z|, q ~ O(1/z) and the equation is dominated by -psi_p z + (1 - psi_p)/q ~ -psi_p z + psi_p z = 0, the correct asymptotic balance for a resolvent. Internally consistent; not independently checkable from the main text.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.content: Theorem 3.1. With $q(z) = \frac{1}{p}\mathrm{Tr}(\mathbf{U} - z\mathbf{I}_p)^{-1}$, $r(z) = \frac{1}{p}\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma^{1/2}\mathbf{W}^T(\mathbf{U} - z\mathbf{I}_p)^{-1}\mathbf{W}\Sigma^{1/2})$, $s(z) = \frac{1}{p}\mathrm{Tr}(\mathbf{W}^T(\mathbf{U} - z\mathbf{I}_p)^{-1}\mathbf{W})$, $\hat{s}(q) = b_t^2\psi_p + 1/q$, $\hat{r}(r,q) = \psi_p a_t^2 e^{-2t}/(1 + a_t^2 e^{-2t}\psi_p r/\psi_n + \psi_p v_t^2 q/\psi_n)$, the three resolvent equations (17)-(19) hold, and $\rho(\lambda) = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+} \frac{1}{\pi}\mathrm{Im}\, q(\lambda + i\varepsilon)$.
results.route_rationale: Rests on random-matrix objects (Stieltjes transforms, Gaussian Equivalence); the Sokhotski-Plemelj sign and internal consistency are checked informally.

math_result.reasoning: Theorem 3.1 states the coupled system of three resolvent equations and the Sokhotski-Plemelj inversion. The Stieltjes transform convention q(z) = (1/p) Tr((U - zI)^{-1}) gives Im q(lambda + i epsilon) = (1/p) sum_i epsilon/((lambda_i - lambda)^2 + epsilon^2) -> pi rho(lambda), so rho = lim (1/pi) Im q(lambda + i epsilon) is correct (no missing minus sign; verified on the single-eigenvalue case q = 1/(lambda_0 - z)). The three equations (17)-(19) are structurally consistent with each other and with the definitions (15)-(16). The theorem rests on random-matrix machinery (GEP, linear pencils) whose derivation is in the SM, so the full claim is not independently checkable from the main text, but no internal contradiction is present.

results.location: 3 Training dynamics of a Random Features Network
results.content: Theorem 3.2 (Informal). Regime I ($\psi_p > \psi_n \gg 1$): $$\rho(\lambda) = \left(1 - \frac{1 + \psi_n}{\psi_p}\right)\delta(\lambda - s_t^2) + \frac{\psi_n}{\psi_p}\rho_1(\lambda) + \frac{1}{\psi_p}\rho_2(\lambda).$$ Regime II ($\psi_n > \psi_p \gg 1$): $$\rho(\lambda) = \left(1 - \frac{1}{\psi_p}\right)\rho_1(\lambda) + \frac{1}{\psi_p}\rho_2(\lambda),$$ where $\rho_1$ is atomless with support $[s_t^2 + v_t^2(1 - \sqrt{\psi_p/\psi_n})^2,\, s_t^2 + v_t^2(1 + \sqrt{\psi_p/\psi_n})^2]$, and $\rho_2$ is the bulk of $\tilde{\mathbf{U}} = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}}[\mathbf{U}]$.
results.route_rationale: Informal spectral statement; the load-bearing algebraic sub-claims (coefficients sum to 1; support interval proper) are formalisable and machine-checked.

lean_result.reasoning: Formalised the load-bearing algebraic sub-claims of the informal Theorem 3.2: (1) Regime I mixture coefficients sum to 1, (2) Regime II mixture coefficients sum to 1, (3) the support of rho_1 is a proper interval (left endpoint <= right endpoint given v_t^2 >= 0 and r = sqrt(psi_p/psi_n) >= 0). All three theorems compile cleanly in Lean 4 (Mathlib v4.33.1); axioms are the standard {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; no sorry. The full spectral statement (delta-mixture, atomless bulks, random-matrix derivation) is not formalisable from the main text and is assessed informally; the coefficient-normalisation algebra that a probability density requires is machine-checked.

summary: Checked all 21 self-contained mathematical objects of the manuscript: 19 numbered equations and Theorems 3.1 and 3.2. The remaining 19 snippets are definitions, model statements, and random-matrix self-consistency equations whose derivation is deferred to the Supplemental Material; all were assessed informally and no error was found: signs in the forward/reverse SDEs, the score-matching objective, the Gaussian-mixture empirical density, the Gamma_t identity, the Sokhotski-Plemelj inversion, and the asymptotic balance of the closing equation all check out.
